sources.extracted_facts: Relivo = open-source multi-namespace MCP server in Go; five namespaces (memory, skills, gsc, producthunt, event) on one HTTP endpoint over Streamable HTTP; every namespace requires X-API-Key before dispatch; memory and event scope each caller to their own rows; event namespace = Kafka over MCP on Confluent Cloud with durable per-caller consumer group; memory = hybrid RAG over Postgres + pgvector; skills = find and download Agent Skills live from GitHub, nothing cached; producthunt = Product Hunt v2 GraphQL over MCP.

Landing + docs copy: 'Point any MCP client at a route and its tools appear'; namespace cards with tool counts; mcp.json config block; feature pillars incl. self-registering mux (cmd/server/main.go never changes) and 'Keyed by default'; 'Nothing is cached; every call reflects live GitHub'; event card: 'Produce to a topic, poll it back through a durable consumer group, and manage topics on Confluent Cloud.'

event namespace mechanics: event_publish stamps an authoritative x-mcp-owner header from the caller's api_key_id; event_consume is a bounded poll that returns only the caller's own records via durable per-caller cursor; Kafka publish returns the partition it landed on and an offset; topic admin gated behind KAFKA_ALLOW_TOPIC_ADMIN; built on the official MCP Go SDK Streamable HTTP transport.

Real run on topic 'go-mcp-events'. Three events published in order: offset 0 skill.acquired (skill frontend-design, acquire-skill into .claude/skills/); offset 1 skill.task (skill awesome-design-skills, acquire-skill, the 'just publish' version with no inline download); offset 2 task.producthunt (generate-file information.md from the producthunt MCP, fetch the top-ranked Product Hunt product). Guidance that reshaped the pattern: 'just publish the task' rather than the producer doing the download/install itself.

sources.extracted_facts: Setup + tool reference from /doc/event: connect by dropping the event route (https://go-mcp-server-latest.onrender.com/event/mcp) into the MCP client's mcp.json with an X-API-Key header; mint the key via Sign in / the Keys page (/doc/keys); one key admits the whole server. event_publish(value, topic, key, headers) returns the partition and offset; same key routes to the same partition. event_consume(topic, from:'group', max, timeout_ms) is a bounded poll with durable group offsets that advance across calls; loop is poll, do the work, poll again; a restarted agent resumes from its committed offset. Security: anyone with produce access can write to the topic, so a payload is a request not a trusted command; a worker should verify claims and escalate rather than run destructive or outward-facing actions on a message's say so.
